samples.summary: POPUP_SELECTOR treats a pointerdown inside ANY role="dialog"/listbox/menu in the app as "the user is working the toolbar", so an unrelated modal interaction can arm a focus release that later routes keystrokes to the canvas
samples.evidence: `isPointerDrivenTarget()` (line 64-70) returns true for a pointerdown anywhere inside `[role="dialog"], [role="menu"], [role="listbox"], [data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]` — not just popups owned by the marked toolbar. Any app-wide modal (share dialog, confirm-delete, shortcuts help) matches. Once `pointerDriven` is latched, the next `focusin` landing on any toolbar button releases focus to `document.body`, at which point the slides document-level keydown rules run: destructive ones (Delete/Backspace element removal, Cmd+Z, and Cmd+V which calls `navigator.clipboard.read()` in `packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:811`) become active. Attacker leverage is weak — this needs the legitimate user's own pointer input, and the clipboard read is a same-user, user-gesture path that logs only errors, never contents (keyboard.ts:832) — so I could not build an exploitation chain; the concern is that the arming condition is broader than the toolbar the hook claims to scope itself to. Tightening `isPointerDrivenTarget` to popups anchored to the marked toolbar (e.g. via the trigger's `aria-controls`/popper root) would keep the release scoped to its stated surface.

samples.summary: Global capture-phase focus release keys off an attribute selector that any DOM in the document can set, so non-app markup could induce blur behaviour
samples.evidence: `TOOLBAR_SELECTOR = "[data-canvas-toolbar]"` is matched against the whole document by document-level capture listeners (lines 108-110). The hook trusts the attribute as an ownership marker, so any element that carries it — injected markup, a third-party embed, or a future surface that renders untrusted HTML — gets its focused button-like descendants blurred to `document.body`. Today the blast radius is nil: I grepped the frontend and the attribute is only set at `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/index.tsx:110` and in the new test, and the only `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in the frontend (`components/ui/chart.tsx:81`) injects CSS from static config, not attributes, so I could not reach the selector with attacker-controlled DOM. Recording it as a hardening note: scoping the listeners to a ref'd toolbar element instead of a document-wide attribute selector removes the trust-the-DOM assumption entirely.
